Hi team —

Attached is the Q3 OKR slate (v2) plus the Launchboard metrics workbook. This is the consolidated version after the cross-org owner workshop last week. Key asks:

- Please review the Governance section (pp. 4-6) — this tightens owner responsibilities and escalation windows.
- Confirm or propose final owner for the "Model Serving Cost per 1M tokens" metric. Current owner listed: Platform/Runtime (Jonas).
- Approve the rollout plan in Appendix B. We need exec ratification to roll into the QBR packet by EOD Friday.

I've also attached a short redline that captures a small scope tightening from Kimberly's team. If you can't approve, please reply with the exact change you want (one-line) so we can iterate quickly.

Attachments: Q3-OKR-slate-v2.pdf, Launchboard-metrics-v1.xlsx, governance-rules-redline.docx

Thanks —

Hannah — thanks for pulling this together. A couple of technical notes from Platform/Runtime:

- "Model Serving Cost per 1M tokens" is fine with me to own, but I want the SLA baseline appended (current p50/p95 latency bands) so the cost metric is evaluated against expected latency SLOs. I'll drop the baseline into the metrics workbook by EOD today.
- On the Launchboard metrics, there's an open data collection gap for quantized inference memory usage (SUP-1823). I've linked the Jira in case the metrics team wants to coordinate.

One suggestion to speed signoff: add a single-line "evaluation rubric" below each objective that lists acceptance criteria (e.g., measurement window, owner, gate). I can draft a template and push to the Drive.

On governance redline: I propose we accept Kimberly's tightening but scope it to "pilot teams" for Q3 rather than org-wide.

Thanks — Jonas

Thanks all — appreciate the quick read. I pushed a 1-line redline into governance-rules-redline.docx to tighten scope for infra change approvals (SecOps + Platform signoff for any kernel/quantization changes affecting production). My ask: keep the approval window at 48 hours for non-blocking changes but require 5-day notice for kernel replacements.

Kimberly's intent is risk reduction; pilot-limited scope sounds reasonable to me as a compromise. If Platform can commit to adding the SLA baseline and the acceptance-rubric template, I'm comfortable approving.

All — I reviewed the thread and attachments. Quick notes:

1) Approve the slate pending the two small changes (Laura timeline tweak + Jonas SLA baseline in the workbook).
2) We should flag the "pilot" language in the executive summary to avoid an accidental org-wide interpretation.
3) Hannah — please include a 1-slide exceptions policy in the QBR packet that explains when an exception path (escalation to exec) is used and by whom.

If the above items are done by close of business Thursday, I will include the slate in the QBR packet for Friday's leadership review.
